playoff.note: Single-leg semi-finals paired 3v6 and 4v5, then a single-leg final; the higher-placed club hosts every match. Winner takes the third promotion place.
Same 3v6 / 4v5 single-leg bracket, winner promoted. This league also runs a relegation play-off (13th and 14th v the two III-liga runners-up that survive round 1, two legs) - see boundary 3-4.

boundaries.note: Ekstraklasa 16th-18th relegated. 1 Liga 1st-2nd promoted directly, 3rd-6th play off for the third place.
1 Liga 16th-18th relegated, so the league holds 18. 2 Liga 1st-2nd promoted directly, 3rd-6th play off for the third place.

Variable boundary: 4 is the floor, 6 the maximum. The champion of each of the four III-liga groups is promoted directly (4, no play-off). The four runners-up enter a two-round play-off: round 1 is a single match with the fixed bracket gr. I v gr. III and gr. IV v gr. II; round 2 is two legs against the 13th and 14th of 2 Liga (II-liga club hosts the second leg). Each tie won by a runner-up swaps one club, so 0-2 extra promotions and 0-2 extra relegations. Group placement is territorial by voivodeship, not a fixed membership; a group that receives a relegated II-liga club sends one extra club down to IV liga (5 instead of 4) to stay at 18.

conflicts.topic: Level 4 is one competition, not four leagues
conflicts.detail: PL31-PL34 are the four territorial groups of a single III liga (72 clubs). Clubs are re-placed between groups every season by voivodeship, and the play-off for promotion pairs groups against each other. Modelling the four rows as independent closed leagues with a fixed 1-up-1-down each is wrong: they share one promotion play-off and their relegation counts vary.

conflicts.topic: 3-4 boundary is not a fixed number
conflicts.detail: 4 direct promotions (group champions) + 0-2 from the runners-up play-off; 4 direct relegations + 0-2 from the same ties. JSON stores the maximum 6 with the 2 variable places marked as playoff places; read 4 as the guaranteed floor.

Legia II Warszawa and Śląsk II Wrocław play in 2 Liga. No reserve team has ever played in the Polish second tier and the historical rule barred reserve teams of Ekstraklasa/1 Liga clubs from promotion to 1 Liga. Treat their promotion to level 2 as blocked, but confirm against the 2026-27 PZPN regulation before hard-coding.

notes: All four database rows (18/18/18/18x4) match the real 2026-27 sizes; the DB levels are correct. Every Polish level is a plain double round-robin (18 clubs = 34 rounds), no split, no carried points, no average-points rule. Season is in progress (mid-November 2026), so promotion/relegation outcomes above are the regulatory rules, not final tables. Level 4 -> IV liga is out of scope. Cups and UEFA competitions excluded.
